title: cycle-note source (kebab-case)
description: Schema for projects/<group>/<name>/docs/cycles/<X.Y>.yaml — the per-cycle execution record filed at the end of each TDD cycle (cycle-orchestration.md §Cycle notes format). Execution-only: read by the orchestrator/reviewer and reviewed by the human at commit-time via diff; NOT rendered into the docs HTML site. additionalProperties:false everywhere so typo'd / unknown keys fail validation loudly.

review-passes.description: One entry per REVIEW pass, INCLUDING passes that returned zero findings — cycle-orchestration.md §Reviewer separation makes this a MUST. Without it a clean APPROVED pass leaves no machine-readable trace of who reviewed it: reviewer-agent-id otherwise lives only inside reviewer-findings[], so a no-findings pass names nobody and the self-review check cannot fire on the case where an accidental self-review is easiest to miss. Still OPTIONAL here because 0 of the 130 notes on record carry one and cycle notes are historical execution records that are never rewritten — validate-cycle-note.mjs instead hard-errors on a note that names no reviewer in EITHER field, and warns when the roster is missing. Because no note on record carries a roster, reviewer-agent-id inside it is held to the strict canonical grammar ($defs/reviewer-pass-id) with none of the legacy tolerance reviewer-findings[] needs.

allOf.$comment: Presence of review-passes[] is what marks a note NEW-style — 0 of the 130 notes on record carry the roster. So a note that carries one is held to the canonical id grammar on BOTH surfaces, not just the roster: without this, a new note could keep naming its reviewers in reviewer-findings[] free prose and the positive constraint would bind only where nobody writes. Legacy notes are untouched by construction, since they have no review-passes[] to trigger the branch.

reviewer-pass-id.description: CANONICAL reviewer identity — the positive constraint that replaced the old `not: [Ss]elf[- _]?[Rr]eview` keyword filter. That filter never rejected anything: the token appears 0 times across the 130 notes on record, while `"orchestrator (this session, reviewed its own GREEN output)"` sailed straight through the minLength:1 field it guarded. Exactly one of two anchored forms, nothing else. (1) WORKFLOW-ISSUED — `wf:<runId>/review-pass-<N>`, or `security-pass-<N>` for the security-tier second pass; e.g. `wf:wf_ac45c2a0-883/review-pass-1`. This is the shape tdd-cycle.js emits mechanically (cycle-orchestration.md §Reviewer separation, `reviewerIdConvention`); <runId> is accepted as [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64} rather than pinned to today's `wf_<8hex>-<3hex>` so a runtime that changes its run-ID format does not falsify every note at once. (2) MANUAL PATH — a bare Agent-tool agent ID, `a` + 16 lowercase hex, e.g. `a3c94389c274c9715`. Only 27 of the 130 notes ran via the workflow; without this branch the roster would be unfillable off-workflow and would go unused, which is the exact defect it exists to close. Role labels, verdicts and pass narration belong in `role` / `verdict` / `findings-count`, never inside the ID.

reviewer-agent-id-legacy.description: Identifier of the agent that performed the pass, as recorded inside `reviewer-findings[]`. Legacy-tolerant ON PURPOSE: 146 of the 248 distinct values across the 130 notes on record are free prose (`"Code Reviewer a03c8edf612e5dd26 (APPROVED, pass 3)"`, `"cr051@session-f3a1ebde"`, `"isc-cycle-1.6 workflow — review:1.6#1 (fresh Code Reviewer…)"`), and cycle notes are historical execution records — they are never rewritten to satisfy a newer schema. So the canonical grammar binds here only where a value CLAIMS to be machine-issued: anything starting `wf:` must match $defs/reviewer-pass-id exactly. All 48 `wf:` values on record already conform, so this can only bite a newly hand-composed one. The `not: self-review` filter is kept as the residual floor on this surface — it is the guard cycle-orchestration.md §Reviewer separation documents as schema-enforced. The tolerance is legacy-only, not permanent: the second `allOf` branch escalates THIS field to the full canonical grammar as soon as the note carries a `review-passes[]` roster, i.e. for every new-style note.
